overall: The AG found the committee violated the OML at its Aug 5, 2010 meeting by discussing topics beyond the cited Purpose 3 in executive session and by the chair failing to make the required declaration; the litigation purpose itself was valid. Matter closed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee entered executive session on Aug 5, 2010 under Purpose 3 (litigation strategy) for a non-permissible reason, since only an investigation and 'possible' litigation were noticed.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the executive session minutes and response of the Committee make clear that at least a portion of the executive session discussion focused on whether the Committee should initiate legal action against a particular individual.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair did not properly invoke Purpose 3; the chair did not declare that an open meeting would harm the body's litigating position.
allegations.key_passage: We note, however, that in reciting Purpose Three, the Chair failed to declare that an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the litigating position of the public body, as required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Executive session discussion covered other topics about the investigated individual (e.g., discipline, criminal matters, confidential reports) that fell outside the cited Purpose 3.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, the Committee's discussion covered a range of other topics — all related to the individual being investigated—that did not fall within Purpose Three.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law

Promptly release to the public the August 5, 2010 executive session minutes and other non-exempt documents once the legal purpose for the executive session has expired (expectation, not a formal order)
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and remind the Committee of its responsibility to follow the required procedures for entering executive session.
